clue.text: Postures for ascents, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says these letters might be arranged some other way, so they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A climbing coach discusses the body positions suited to different climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Stances are the positions a body is held in, the same as postures.

clue.text: Gossip caused by shoe found outside front of chamber

indicators.note: found outside says the shoe's letters sit around the next piece

parts.note: a sandal is a kind of shoe

indicators.note: front of picks just the opening letter of the word chamber

explanation.surface: Tongues wag after a shoe turns up outside a bedroom door.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a juicy story that sets tongues wagging, which is gossip.

clue.text: One satisfied with change around something in the cockpit

indicators.note: around says the word for change wraps itself about the other pieces

parts.note: to alter is to change
one is the Roman numeral I
met, as in met a demand, means satisfied

explanation.surface: Someone content with a change potters about a plane's flight deck.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter is a height gauge found among a pilot's instruments.

clue.text: Mates finish playing this

parts.note: reads like friends wrapping up a game, but checkmate is what ends this board game

explanation.surface: Friends stop playing a game together.
explanation.definitionFit: A game of chess ends when one player delivers checkmate.

clue.text: Firm nurtures the leader with a stiff upper lip

indicators.note: nurtures suggests holding something close, so the firm's word holds the next letter

parts.note: solid means firm

indicators.note: the leader of the word the is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A company fosters a boss who never shows emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stolid is unemotional and impassive, keeping a stiff upper lip.

clue.text: One from the country has vegetables planted in the middle

parts.note: peas are vegetables

indicators.note: in the middle takes the central letters of the word planted, dropping its outer pairs

explanation.surface: A rural dweller has vegetables sown in the centre of a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a farm worker of the countryside.

clue.text: Around end of hostilities pelted a new base

indicators.note: Around says the rearranged letters surround the next piece
new indicates the letters of pelted and a are made into a fresh order
end of picks the last letter of hostilities

explanation.surface: When fighting ended, someone threw stones at a new plinth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns PELTED A into PEDETAL, and 'Around' puts the S from the end of 'hostilities' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base on which a statue or column stands.

clue.text: Wren, perhaps, flying the arctic

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are sent off in all directions and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A wren, a small bird, flies across the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral; 'Wren' looks like the bird but is the architect.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Wren is a famous designer of buildings, an example of the profession.

clue.text: Fib in an exciting film based in space

indicators.note: in says the word for fib goes inside the word an

parts.note: a fib is a lie

explanation.surface: A fib is told in a thrilling science-fiction movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien is the 1979 science-fiction horror film set on a spaceship.

clue.text: The heartless have swords in tents

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter of the word the

parts.note: epees are fencing swords

explanation.surface: Cold-hearted people keep their swords inside their tents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The heartless' reads as cruel people, but it means a word with its centre removed; epees are the fencing swords tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Teepees are conical tents of the Plains peoples of North America.

clue.text: When training, redcoat makes movement

indicators.note: training suggests drilling into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A British soldier in training goes through his drill.
explanation.walkthrough: A redcoat is an old British soldier; 'movement' looks like drill but means an artistic style.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is a 1920s and 1930s design movement.

clue.text: The Latin scholar must refuse

definitions.meaning: a student of Latin has to inflect nouns through their cases
to say no to an offer

explanation.surface: A classics student has to say no.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflecting a Latin noun through its cases is the grammar sense, and turning down an offer is the everyday one.

clue.text: Cooking iced scones etc. I'm displaying it?

indicators.note: displaying suggests the letters are laid out afresh in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A baker shows off iced scones and other bakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic science is the school subject of cookery and housekeeping.

clue.text: Allow prince Henry to be very nasty indeed

parts.note: to let is to allow
Hal is Shakespeare's name for Prince Henry, later Henry V

explanation.surface: Letting Prince Henry loose would be extremely unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deadly is about as nasty as it gets.

clue.text: What a sailor might do to a ship when taking on English hermit

parts.words: What a sailor might do to a ship
parts.note: a sailor might moor a vessel in place with a heavy weight dropped to the seabed, said as a verb with an object

explanation.surface: A seaman's task with a vessel involves taking on board an English recluse.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorite is a religious recluse living apart from the world.

clue.text: Extremely hungry birds outside old university

indicators.note: outside says the birds' word goes round the university's letters

parts.note: ravens are birds
OU is the Open University; old here simply decorates it

explanation.surface: Starving birds gather outside an old college.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenous means famished, desperately wanting food.

clue.text: Musical about a river upset agent

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the whole string upside down, reading it from the bottom

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
re means about, concerning
the Po is a river in Italy

explanation.surface: A stage show about a river troubles a secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns EVITA RE PO backwards as one string.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a secret agent or spy.

clue.text: Damage a short shoe in race

parts.note: to mar is to damage

indicators.note: short means the shoe's word loses its last letter

parts.note: a thong is a flip-flop style shoe

explanation.surface: Ruining a flimsy sandal partway through a long run.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a long-distance running race.

clue.text: Traitor's act with paint

definitions.note: the possessive here stands for traitor is, so a single defector is defined

parts.note: a turn is an act on stage
a coat is a layer of paint

explanation.surface: A turncoat's deed involves daubing paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat is someone who switches sides, a defector.

clue.text: Very warm without river current

indicators.note: without means the river's letter is taken out

parts.note: tropical means very warm

explanation.surface: A hot climate lacks any flowing water.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical news is current, of present interest.

clue.text: Underline result of being overworked

definitions.meaning: the strain felt by someone with too much to do

explanation.surface: Someone stresses the effects of working too hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise is the verb sense; strain and tension from overwork is the noun sense.

clue.text: Sure, on the Sabbath Arabs might be found here

parts.note: stable means sure, steady
S stands for Sunday, the Christian Sabbath

explanation.surface: On a holy day, Arab people may be found here.
explanation.walkthrough: Arabs here are the horse breed, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Stables house horses, and the Arab is a breed of horse.

clue.text: Prizes for the soldiers

explanation.surface: Awards are given out to the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To prise something open is to lever it, while the armed services are military troops.

clue.text: Unwelcome person in Rome

parts.note: someone not wanted, described in the Latin language of the Romans

explanation.surface: A visitor to the Italian capital is not wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase names someone not welcome, especially a diplomat expelled by a host country.

clue.text: Bible lesson on race is broadcast again

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject
a run is a race

explanation.surface: A Bible lesson about a race gets a repeat airing.
explanation.definitionFit: To rerun a programme is to show it once more.

clue.text: Plant that can cause blood around end, of fingers

indicators.note: around says the blood's word wraps the final letter

parts.note: gore is spilt blood

indicators.note: end picks the final letter of fingers

explanation.surface: A prickly shrub can make fingertips bleed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub.

clue.text: Sailors and I enter club from a county

indicators.note: enter says the sailors and I go inside the club

parts.note: a cosh is a short heavy club
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Navy men and I join a club in a shire.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornish means coming from Cornwall, a county in south-west England.

clue.text: Warm drink

explanation.surface: A hot beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly greeting is the adjective sense; a fruit squash is the noun sense.

clue.text: It's light to carry

parts.note: reads as something not heavy, but light means illumination you hold in your hand

explanation.surface: Something is easy to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp.

clue.text: They make bent pins for cooking

definitions.text: They make bent pins for cooking

parts.words: They make bent pins for cooking
parts.note: suggests people bending pins, but these are themselves pins used to hold meat over heat

explanation.surface: Workers twist pins in a kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Skewers are metal or wooden pins that hold food while it cooks.
